title: SGHateCheck: Functional Tests for Detecting Hate Speech in Low-Resource Languages of Singapore

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating fine-tuned large language models on the SGHateCheck functional test suite, which uses templated text statements (both hateful and non-hateful) to measure hate speech detection F1 scores for targets such as seniors.

Evaluating fine-tuned large language models on the SGHateCheck functional test suite using localized text templates to measure detection capabilities for hate speech targeting mentally ill and physically disabled individuals.
Testing the F1 scores and accuracy of language models on functional test cases containing directed hate speech and contrastive non-hateful statements targeting women and gender identities.
Using the SGHateCheck diagnostic dataset to evaluate model performance (F1 scores) on detecting hateful versus non-hateful functional test cases targeting homosexuals and transsexuals.
Measuring the detection performance of LLMs on targeted hate speech and contrastive examples directed at immigrants using a suite of multilingual functional tests.
Assessing model accuracy and F1 scores using specific functional test templates containing slurs, profanity, and implicit derogation targeted at racial groups in Singapore (Chinese, Indians, Malay).
Evaluating LLM hate speech detection performance across four languages using functional test cases targeting specific religious groups (Buddhist, Christian, Hindu, Muslim).

Comparing hate speech detection accuracy and F1 scores of LLMs across English, Singlish, Mandarin, Malay, and Tamil to reveal systematic detection gaps and vulnerabilities in low-resource and regional language contexts.
